title: A principal localization of a global complete intersection over a field is a global complete intersection
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $T$ a global complete intersection over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]. Let $g\in T$ and let $T_g$ be the localization of $T$ at the multiplicative set $\{1,g,g^2,\dots\}$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away], a $k$-algebra through $k\to T\to T_g$. Then $T_g$ is a global complete intersection over $k$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00SA (lemma-localize-lci, line 35856), part (1), proof lines 35868-35881; tag verified in stacks-project/tags/tags (00SA,algebra-lemma-localize-lci)

proof.text: If $T_g=0$, it is a global complete intersection by the zero-ring clause of [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]. Otherwise choose, from the global complete intersection hypothesis, a surjective $k$-algebra homomorphism $\alpha:P=k[x_1,\dots,x_n]\to T$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] with kernel $I=(f_1,\dots,f_c)$ and $\dim T=n-c$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. The induced map $P/I\to T$, $[u]\mapsto\alpha(u)$, is a $k$-algebra isomorphism: it is surjective with zero kernel, so from now on use it to identify $T$ with the displayed quotient $P/I$. Fix a polynomial $h\in P$ with $\alpha(h)=g$; such a lift exists because $\alpha$ is surjective.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00SA (lemma-localize-lci), lines 35868-35876; Definition Tag 00S9 (definition-lci-field), lines 35817-35831

proof.text: Since $T_g\neq0$, its spectrum has a point $q$. By [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion], the localization map gives a homeomorphism $u:\operatorname{Spec}T_g\to D(g)$ onto the open subspace $D(g)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}T$. Let $p=u(q)$. The homeomorphism restricts, for every open neighborhood $V$ of $q$, to a homeomorphism $V\to u(V)$ onto an open neighborhood of $p$, and its inverse takes every open neighborhood of $p$ in $D(g)$ back to one of $q$; [lem-weil-pbc-homeomorphism-krull-dimension] gives $\dim V=\dim u(V)$. Taking minima over these paired neighborhoods [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point] yields $\dim_q\operatorname{Spec}T_g=\dim_p D(g)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-open-subspace] this is $\dim_p\operatorname{Spec}T$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-global-complete-intersection-equidimensional] the latter is $n-c$ for every such $p$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions] to the nonempty space $\operatorname{Spec}T_g$: all its local dimensions are $n-c$, hence $\dim T_g=n-c$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension].

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00SA (lemma-localize-lci), lines 35871-35876, using the paragraph after Definition Tag 00S9 (definition-lci-field), lines 35833-35849

proof.text: Let $y$ be one new variable and define $\beta:P[y]\to T_g$ by $\beta|_P=(T\to T_g)\circ\alpha$ and $\beta(y)=g^{-1}$. The coefficientwise map $\alpha[y]:P[y]\to T[y]$ is surjective with kernel $I P[y]$ by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-coefficient-map-kernel]. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-away-polynomial-quotient], evaluation $\lambda:T[y]\to T_g$ at $y=g^{-1}$ is surjective with kernel $(gy-1)T[y]$. Thus $\beta=\lambda\circ\alpha[y]$ is surjective. For $u\in\ker\beta$, write $\alpha[y](u)=(gy-1)v$ and lift $v$ to $v'\in P[y]$; then $u-(hy-1)v'\in I P[y]$. Conversely $I P[y]$ and $hy-1$ map to zero. Hence $\ker\beta=(f_1,\dots,f_c,hy-1)$ and $T_g\cong k[x_1,\dots,x_n,y]/(f_1,\dots,f_c,hy-1)$ as $k$-algebras.

proof.text: The presentation in step 3 has $n+1$ variables and $c+1$ displayed generators. Step 2 gives $\dim T_g=n-c=(n+1)-(c+1)$. Therefore it meets the nonzero clause of [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field], proving that $T_g$ is a global complete intersection; together with step 1 this covers both cases.

split_report.summary: Checked the statement against Stacks Algebra Lemma 00SA (lemma-localize-lci) and the complete-intersection definition 00S9. The proof handles the zero localization by the definition; for the nonzero case it extracts a presentation, gets the unchanged dimension n-c from the equidimensionality, open-subspace local-dimension and supremum nodes, calculates the kernel of P[y] -> T_g from two existing polynomial localization leaves, and counts n+1 variables and c+1 equations. One exact Mathlib leaf records invariance of global topological Krull dimension under homeomorphism; applying it to neighborhoods justifies invariance of local dimension.
